own_solution.law: Projectile motion: t = 2v sin(theta)/g and R = v cos(theta)t = v² sin(2theta)/g. Thus R = 400 sin(70°)/9.8.
assumptions: Launch and landing occur at the same elevation.
The ball follows an unobstructed ballistic trajectory.
For a prelaunch direction adjustment, 35° is interpreted as the angle before adjustment.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9D35 and TC550 specify an indefinite 'few degrees', whereas their corresponding earlier-trial and ramp variants specify 14°, violating the required preservation of number and unit.
defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: TFDC7 does not establish whether the direction adjustment precedes the current launch or follows it, allowing different launch conditions and ranges.

counterexamples: For TFDC7, lowering the launch direction before the current shot gives an angle of 21° and a range of 27.31145332 m; lowering the launcher after the ball has departed leaves its 35° trajectory and 38.35480085 m range unchanged.
notes: The base problem has the standard unique projectile-range solution. TFDC7 is provisionally assigned R under the interpretation that the adjustment occurs before the current launch; its alternative chronological reading is D. Earlier trials do not affect the current shot, and the adjacent ramp has no stated interaction with the ball. T3E32 and TFC29 preserve 14° while changing the trial attachment; TFDC7 and T9417 preserve 14° while changing the object attachment. The 'few degrees' variants fail the numerical matching requirement.
